sample_unit: nucleic acid test reports (with 285 introduced errors)

links.outcome: Reproducibility of GPT error identification across three repeated runs
links.effect: Pairwise comparisons of the same GPT model's outputs across three repeated runs showed almost perfect agreement (kappa 0.912 to 0.996).
links.quote: The pairwise comparisons of the same GPT model's outputs across three repeated runs showed almost perfect agreement (kappa [min, max]: 0.912, 0.996).

links.outcome: GPT error detection agreement and speed compared with senior scientists and interns
links.effect: GPT models agreed substantially to almost perfectly with SMLS (kappa 0.778-0.837), moderately lower with MLI (0.632-0.696), and read reports faster than both (p<0.001).
links.quote: GPT models exhibited substantial to almost perfect agreement with SMLS in detecting total errors (kappa [min, max]: 0.778, 0.837).

screen.reason: Evaluates the diagnostic accuracy/performance of GPT models (4o, o1, o1 mini) in detecting synthetically introduced errors in lab reports and generating treatment recommendations, compared to human experts. It does not test a deployment practice or organizational safeguard.
